relationship.translation_notes: All terms are monetary flows over one period in the same currency.

limitations: This aggregate identity is not a household-only disposable income measure.

models.title: Government saving with gross taxes and transfers
models.summary: The owner defines government saving as tax revenue less government purchases and transfers.

relationship.original_equation: Government saving = gross taxes − transfers − government purchases
relationship.locator: Measuring Private/Public Income and Saving; Uses of National Saving
relationship.translation_notes: All terms are monetary flows over one period in the same currency.

variables.context: Same economy, reporting currency and accounting period
Same economy, reporting currency and accounting period
Same economy, reporting currency and accounting period
Same economy, reporting currency and accounting period

assumptions: Taxes are gross, transfers include government net interest paid to the private sector or separately omitted net interest is zero, and purchases exclude transfers.
All flows are consistently measured for the same government and period.
limitations: Negative government saving is a deficit under this simplified definition.
The university notes distinguish transfers and interest; their displayed expanded public-saving line omits G, but its immediately preceding definition NGI minus G supports the expression.

models.title: Net exports from sectoral saving and investment with gross taxes
models.summary: The owner derives a sectoral balance with transfers and explicitly treats current account as net exports in a simplified setting.

relationship.original_equation: Net exports = private saving − investment + taxes − government purchases − transfers
relationship.locator: Measuring Private/Public Income and Saving; Uses of National Saving
relationship.translation_notes: All terms are same-period monetary flows in a common currency.

assumptions: Transfers include government net interest to the private sector, or the omitted interest is zero, and taxes are gross.
Net foreign factor income and net external current transfers are zero or outside this simplified identity.
Private saving, investment and government flows use consistent national-accounting boundaries.
limitations: Net exports alone is not the full current account when cross-border primary income or current transfers are material.
This expands the existing transfer-excluded sectoral identity; do not subtract transfers a second time when taxes are already net.
